title: Agent Debugging & Decision Tracing
description: Debug AI agent failures, trace decision chains, and build replay tooling for iterative agent development.

data.text: The Black Box Problem: Why Agents Are Hard to Debug

Unlike traditional applications where you can set breakpoints and step through code, AI agents have non-deterministic, LLM-mediated decision paths. When an agent fails, you can't simply inspect a stack trace. You need to capture the full decision chain — every thought, action, and observation — and provide tooling to replay, inspect, and analyze them.
Decision Tracing: Capturing Thought -> Action -> Observation

Every agent step produces three pieces of information: the agent's internal reasoning (thought/prompt sent to LLM), the tool call it decided to make (action), and the result from the environment (observation). Capturing all three into a structured trace allows post-hoc analysis of why the agent took a particular path.

data.title: Agent Step Tracing with Full Context Capture
data.content: Capturing thought, action, and observation for each agent step:

data.text: Agent traces enable powerful debugging workflows: replay a session in isolation, compare two agent versions on the same input, simulate different tool responses, and analyze failure patterns. A dedicated inspector UI shows each step as a card with the thought, action, observation, and resulting trace.

data.title: Agent Session Replay API
data.content: An ASP.NET Core controller for replaying agent sessions:

data.text: Store traces in a queryable format (JSON with indexed metadata). Add correlation IDs that thread through the entire agent session, including tool calls and external API calls. This lets you search for all traces where a specific tool was called or where the agent made more than N steps.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Capture thought (prompt), action (tool call), and observation (result) for every agent step
Structured traces enable post-hoc analysis and failure debugging
Replay tooling allows comparing agent runs, simulating tool responses, and root cause analysis
Highlight failed steps in the inspector to guide debugging
Thread correlation IDs through all components for end-to-end traceability
data.takeaway: Agent debugging replaces the stack trace with the decision trace. Capturing every step's reasoning, action, and observation makes agent behavior explainable and debuggable.
